query_text: Does it matter what we eat?

content.text:
Yes—it matters a lot, but not in a “you must eat perfectly” way.

What we eat affects:

- **Energy and mood:** Meals with enough protein, fiber-rich carbs, and healthy fats tend to keep blood sugar steadier, which can help energy and concentration.
- **Long-term health:** Eating patterns rich in vegetables, fruits, beans/lentils, whole grains, nuts, seeds, fish, and unsaturated fats are linked with lower risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and some other chronic diseases.
- **Gut health:** Fiber feeds beneficial gut bacteria and supports digestion.
- **Body composition:** Calories matter for weight change, but food quality affects fullness, nutrition, and how easy it is to maintain habits.
- **Performance and recovery:** Protein, carbohydrates, hydration, and micronutrients all influence exercise, sleep, healing, and immune function.

A practical way to think about it: **most of the time, build meals around minimally processed foods**—protein, plants, whole-food carbohydrates, and healthy fats—while leaving room for foods you simply enjoy.

For example, a solid meal might be:

> salmon or tofu + rice/potatoes + vegetables + olive oil/avocado/nuts

But one meal won’t make or break your health. **Patterns over weeks and months matter more than any single food.**
